Amoris

A downloadable game for Windows

"I’m scared. I’m terrified. I’m sad… but I won’t give up.

 I’ll find you, Camilo… I swear I will. You’re here!"

You play as an 11-year-old girl searching for her missing brother in an unknown world. To find him, she’ll have to explore the strange world around her, solve puzzles, and push forward despite everything standing in her way.


About the Game

Amoris - is a psychological horror game where you’ll have to solve puzzles, explore a mysterious world, uncover its secrets, read through a diary, and piece together what really happened.

This is a story-driven game filled with puzzles of varying difficulty. Explore the world with your friends as you search for your brother, who has disappeared into an unknown world.

Explore the mysterious world with a Strange Magnifying Glass that reveals hidden messages when you look through it. Sophia's diary records important events that happen throughout her journey.

Listen to her inner voice to hear what she’s thinking.

Your actions have consequences. What you do will determine how the story ends.


Warning

The game contains sudden loud sounds, flashing images, scenes involving blood, and references to violence.

Features

  • Lots of story-driven dialogue
  • A strong focus on puzzles, exploration, and story
  • Unique mechanics: Diary, Strange Magnifying Glass, and Inner Voice
  • Lots of original soundtracks
  • Large locations to explore
  • Plenty of important story scenes

Playtime

Approximately 4–5 hours

Developer's Note

Hi everyone!

This is my first game, and it means a lot to me. I really hope you enjoy it!I spent about 1.5 years developing the game, and I made it entirely on my own.

My composer helped me create most of the ambient tracks and music for the game, while Matshar composed the character themes.

I’d really appreciate it if you could leave a review after playing. Your feedback helps me continue improving the game and work toward future updates and new versions.

Thank you for playing!


Follow the Game

You can follow the game at @XiaoNur_Amoris.

You can also subscribe and follow me on YouTube, where I’ll be posting trailers, gameplay clips, and other updates about the game.

casual_entity12 hours ago(+1)

One of the most in-depth and amazing character-driven stories I’ve experienced in a game. It managed to make me instantly invested and genuinely addicted within the first 30 minutes, to the point where I just wanted to complete the entire game in one sitting. The mechanics were also incredibly smooth and satisfying.

I’d genuinely give this game a 4/5 overall. The only reason I didn’t give it a perfect score is because I felt the ending was a little weak. I was expecting some kind of involvement from the demon, or perhaps a storyline where the mother becomes possessed and the player has to find a way to free her. Something along those lines could have added another hour of gameplay and potentially opened the door for multiple endings.But honestly the biggest highlight for me was the puzzles.

Unlike many indie games where you sometimes have to bang your head against a wall just to progress through a small portion of the story, these puzzles were clean, well-thought-out and actually fun to solve. They complemented the story instead of getting in the way of it, which made the entire experience feel incredibly satisfying.

Overall, this was a genuinely enjoyable and memorable experience that completely made my day. Thank you for creating such a great game. I sincerely hope you continue making games like this—or even consider creating a sequel—because you have my utmost respect and support.

I’ve been wanting to play the prototype one for a while now, then I noticed while scrolling you finally released the full game of it, so I ended up playing it, despite some inconveniences happened before playing. And I’m happy to say I enjoyed it! This is probably another one of the better/best RPG Maker games I’ve played, specifically something more leaning towards as a classic RPG Maker Horror. I enjoyed the cast of characters and their characterization as well. Oh one thing I didn’t mention in the description, I do like the magnifying glass for secrets, which is really neat (I wish there was more usage of it, tho probably there was more that I likely missed, which I might still check in the future). The areas and puzzles are really cool (only two puzzles I think I have issues/least favorite), and really reminds me of ib. Music is really great as well. Overall, I enjoyed it, despite the issues (again, couple of puzzle/s, I think there is an issue in a certain part of story, I just think I don’t have words/couldn’t come up atm, what I really want to say, and there are some part that are untranslated/one of the same thoughts got bugged back into RUS language.) Regardless, the pros/positives of this game, outweigh the negatives/cons. Excellent job for first full game, and good luck for future endeavors.
